lede:
Question. Can an open line reader that runs on this laptop (Kraken 7.1 with the OpenITI printed-Arabic model) read Mandumah's pages, and how much does teaching it on our own lines help?

Out of the box it is 3 to 12 times worse than Azure: 3.6 characters in 100 wrong on modern born-digital lines (Azure 1.0), and a quarter of experiment 19's judged scan words wrong (Azure 2 in 100).

Taught on 13,000 lines cut from born-digital PDFs (whose text is exact) and 22,000 real scan lines read by Azure, it gets close to Azure on modern print (1.3–1.5 in 100) and stays good on scan-like copies (1.4–2.1), but on real scans it is still 4 to 8 times Azure: 15 judged words in 100 wrong (Azure 2), body text 4.3 (Azure 1.1); whole scanned pages 13.4 → 8.2 characters in 100 different from Azure's reading.

A small VLM (PaddleOCR-VL) reads single lines about as well, but on whole pages it leaves out and invents text.

Teaching the line finder on 400 scanned pages (Azure's line positions as the lesson, never a held-out journal) cut lines run together across columns 2.4 → 0.6 in 100 and missed lines 2.9 → 1.9, and whole scanned pages went from 8.2 to 6.5 characters in 100 different from Azure. A targeted round for old prints and vowelled lines (half an epoch, on this CPU) did not help. On the owner's two finished gold pages: Azure 0.8, fine-tuned Kraken 2.7–2.8 on the lines, 7.3 → 6.0 on the whole pages.
seg_text:
Kraken finds lines with a network that draws each line's baseline. Out of the box it already finds 93 of every 100 of Azure's lines on experiment 19's 139 scanned pages; its faults are lines run together across two columns (2.4%), lines missed (2.9%) and lines cut in two (1.6%). It was fine-tuned on 400 scanned pages of 290 documents (pages of experiment 19's journals and of every journal experiment 34 holds out were never used), with Azure's line positions as the lesson and the baseline found in the ink (the densest row of each line, where Arabic letters join). This ran on this laptop's CPU, 3 epochs in 3 h 15 min, because uploads to the rented GPUs crawled that night.

Below: Azure's lines (pale blue boxes), kraken's default line finder (red baselines) and the fine-tuned one (green). Two pages where it helped most, and the page where it did worst. The test is against Azure's lines (silver), so a finder that learned Azure's habits is favoured; the owner's two gold pages agree with the direction (7.3 → 6.0 characters in 100 on whole pages).
vlm_text:
PaddleOCR-VL-0.9B, the model card's own recipe (prompt OCR:, greedy), on 60 real-scan lines (7 per kind of word) and 10 scanned pages, scored only. Nothing was tuned on these items. It took three tries to run at all: the current model code needs a transformers version that the card does not name (4.55, 5.0 and 5.19 failed; revision 7faba727 of 2025-12-11 with transformers 4.57.1 runs). Three of the ten pages did not finish inside the 25-minute cap.

Lines: the judged word was wrong 16 times in 60 (Kraken 15, Azure 1). Pages (7 finished): the VLM left out 30% of Azure's words and 44% of its own words are not in Azure's reading, against 11% / 11% for Kraken; one page ran to the 4,096-token cap writing fully vowelled words that are not on the page.
findings:
• Improved: everything that looks like the training print. Born-digital lines 3.6 → 1.3–1.5 characters in 100 (Azure 1.0); scan-like copies 9.0 → 1.4–2.1; Latin lines 61 → 2–3 (the Arabic model had no Latin letters before).
  • Improved, but far from Azure: real scans. Judged words 24.5 → 15.2 in 100 wrong (Azure 2.0); footnotes 17 → 10; first-page titles 32 → 16–22; old prints (before 2000) 22 → 16. Adding 22,000 real scan lines read by Azure (round B) helped most where born-digital lines cannot teach: old print and footnotes.
  • Did not improve much: body text of real scans (5.4 → 4.3, Azure 1.1), headings in decorative type (59 → 47–49), vowelled lines (14 → 11 for Kraken; worse for PP-OCRv6), numbers in tables.
  • Two engines, two strengths: Kraken's classic network is better on old print, vowelled lines, footnotes and numbers; the newer PP-OCRv6 on modern print, titles, running heads and Latin.
  • Finding the lines: fine-tuning the line finder cut lines run together 2.4 → 0.6 in 100 and missed lines 2.9 → 1.9 (cut in two: 1.6 → 2.0, extra lines 183 → 235), and lowered whole-page differences from Azure 8.2 → 6.5 in 100 (pre-2000 9.1 → 7.4).
  • Round C (old prints, footnotes, vowelled) did not help: half an epoch on this CPU with all 4,600 pre-1970 lines, small-print lines and 1,500 synthetic vowelled Quran lines left real-scan words where they were (16.8 in 100), pre-1970 words slightly worse (15.1 → 16.1; round B 12.8) and vowelled words worse (12.2 → 13.4). Synthetic lines in modern typefaces do not teach old vowelled print.
  • The cheapest next gain is more real-scan lines. Azure's readings are free training data; round B used 22,000 lines from 269 documents. Old typefaces need their own lines.
caveats:
• Born-digital lines are easier than old scans, and the born-digital test is print from 2000–2025 only.
  • Documents whose PDF text was broken were left out by agreement with Azure (whole documents only, never single lines' text); this favours documents Azure reads well, so Azure's 1.0 may flatter it.
  • Real-scan lines and pages are scored against Azure's reading (silver): Azure's own errors count against Kraken. Only the judged words (2,894) are checked on the ink.
  • Round B's scan lines came from 32 journals that experiment 34 later held out for its yardstick (the rule came after the run), so the round-B models must not be scored on the yardstick. Round A, round C and the line finder never saw one of those journals.
  • The numbers row (tables, page numbers) depends on how digits are ordered inside right-to-left lines; read it with care.
  • The VLM test is a smoke test: 60 lines and 7 pages, one model, one prompt.
  • One training run on this machine's CPU was stopped by the memory guard; GPU rounds were short (35–60 minutes) and could go further.
  • The owner's gold pages: only two were finished (47 lines, both from experiment 19's documents); a direction, not a measurement.
compute: On this laptop's CPU, fine-tuning reads about 2.7 lines a second whatever the number of threads (an epoch of 27,000 line images takes about 3 hours); on a rented RTX 5090 the same epoch takes 95 seconds (Kraken) or 4 minutes (PP-OCRv6). The night's limit was not the GPU but this machine's upload to the rented machines: 0.02–0.17 MB/s to every host (1.1 MB/s to Cloudflare), so the line finder and round C trained on this CPU instead.
spend_note: GPU total $2.64 of the $10 cap (Vast.ai credit $23.02 → $20.38). What it bought: rounds A and B (both engines) and the VLM smoke test. Five rentals did no work: uploads too slow (four), one host stuck loading its image. No paid API.
gold_text: Two pages were finished by the owner when this ran: 0005-055-003-004 p8 (صحيفة التربية, 2004) and 0018-010-003-002 p3 (مجلة التربية الحديثة, 1937); 47 lines of body text. Each gold line's box was cut from the yardstick's own page image and read by every model; Azure's reading is the yardstick's Azure draft of that line. Scoring only: nothing was tuned on these pages, and neither page's journal gave any training line.
